`class IntegerSignal`<br/>
**Extends:** [`Signal<Integer>`](/reference/signals/signal/)<br/>
**Package:** `dev.joid.lib.signal.impl.primitive` · **Module:** `core` · **Source:** [IntegerSignal.java](https://github.com/Zeldown/JOID/blob/main/core/src/main/java/dev/joid/lib/signal/impl/primitive/IntegerSignal.java)

Signal of an `int` with arithmetic that writes its result, for counters, scores and indexes.

## Description

It works like [`Signal`](/reference/signals/signal/); each operation reads the value, computes and writes the result, which notifies the listeners when it differs.
The operations follow the Java `int` rules: they overflow without error and `divide` rounds toward zero.
Called from another thread, an operation applies on the render thread to the value the signal holds then, so concurrent increments add up.

### divide

`this divide(int value)` <span class="joid-qualifier">fluent</span>

**Throws:**

- `IllegalArgumentException`: The IntegerSignal of value … cannot be divided by 0, check the divisor before calling divide(...)

Divides the value by `value`, rounding toward zero, then returns this signal.
A divisor of `0` throws an `IllegalArgumentException` at the call and leaves the value unchanged.
